question: What is the exact value of the speed of light in vacuum, in metres per second?
answer: The speed of light in vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second [1][2][5]. The value is exact because, by international agreement, the metre is defined as the distance light travels in vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second [1]. That definition dates from 1983, so the value carries no measurement uncertainty and better experiments now only refine how precisely the metre is realized [1][2].
